artworks.title: Electra at the Tomb of Agamemnon
artworks.description: Leighton's Electra stands alone at her father's grave, black drapery clutched to her breast, the Mycenaean tomb a cold vertical behind her. The canvas freezes the Sophoclean princess in the long vigil before Orestes returns — grief turned into a vow. Oil on canvas.

artworks.title: Electra Receiving the Ashes of Her Brother Orestes
artworks.description: Wicar stages the cruel trick of Sophocles' Electra: the urn said to hold Orestes' ashes is placed in her hands while the living brother stands unrecognized beside her. The painting turns the recognition scene into neoclassical pathos — the sister who has kept the house of Atreus awake for revenge. Oil on canvas.

artworks.title: Mourning Electra
artworks.description: Tischbein's grieving princess sits in dark classical dress, eyes lowered over the murdered king's memory. The German neoclassical portrait isolates Electra as the Oresteia's mourner-in-chief — the daughter who will not let Agamemnon's death grow quiet. Oil on canvas.

artworks.title: Orestes and Electra
artworks.description: Fagan pairs the siblings in a quiet clasp: Electra and the returned Orestes before the matricide that will avenge Agamemnon. The National Trust canvas gives visual form to the Libation Bearers' reunion — conspiracy and recognition held in one embrace. Oil on canvas.

artworks.title: Electra and Orestes at the Tomb of Agamemnon (Melian relief)
artworks.description: This Melian terracotta relief in the Louvre (MNB 906) shows Electra and Orestes meeting at Agamemnon's tomb — the recognition that opens Aeschylus's Libation Bearers. The fifth-century plaque is among the earliest surviving images of the sister who keeps vigil until her brother comes home to kill. Louvre, Paris.

films.title: Electra
films.description: Irene Papas' Electra is Cacoyannis' black-and-white Oresteia: the daughter who will not forget Agamemnon, waiting in rags for Orestes and the axe.

music.title: Elektra
music.description: Strauss and Hofmannsthal compress the revenge into one savage evening: Electra dancing herself to death when the house of Atreus is finally paid in blood.
